name: Rena's Central Treasury Vault
description:
- The Vault lies five levels beneath the Council Chambers, constructed directly into the bedrock of Rena’s central hill.
- It is tri-faction controlled, meaning no single faction can access its deepest level without consensus or shared keys.
- Built during the early rise of the city—shortly after the fall of the Velrathi Empire—the Vault blends ancient imperial magic with newer enchantments, mechanical traps, and bureaucratic redundancies.
- Its internal structure resembles a layered spiral, with increasing security the deeper one goes, culminating in the Core Vault, where magical artifacts, ancient relics, debt ledgers, and vaultmaster tokens are kept.
notes:
Access Structure and Entry Flow
1. Surface-Level Entry Gate (Restricted)
	• Access begins in a sealed wing of the Council Hall, through a hidden lift guarded at all times by Crimson Guard officers and construct sentries.
	• The door requires three keys to activate:
		○ A blood-etched coin from the Golden Ledger
		○ A spell-token attuned to a Sigil officer
		○ A runed command badge from a Crimson Guard captain
	• The lift descends 500 feet and can only move if all three tokens are present and active.

2. Security Checkpoint Alpha (Entry Tunnel)
	• A narrow, smooth obsidian hallway roughly 50 feet long with cylindrical sentry glyphs embedded in the ceiling.
	• Divination traps line the walls, detecting illusion, shapeshifting, and invisibility.
	• Pressure plates trigger binding arcane chains if stepped on out of turn.
	• A guardian golem crafted from gold and steel stands watch at the end; it recognizes authorized personnel via soulprint resonance—if soulprint does not match, the golem becomes hostile.

3. Security Checkpoint Beta (Puzzle Gate)
(Designed by the Golden Ledger)
	• A long room with a rotating chamber of mechanical and magical locks:
		○ Includes a riddle-based vault dial, requiring answers drawn from Rena’s economic history
		○ A contractual barrier must be “signed” via arcane oath; lying or forging the signature results in the signer's soul being trapped temporarily in a mirrored prison.
		○ Failing the puzzle three times resets the entire sequence and alerts the Triumvirate.
	• A complex time-based puzzle must also be solved, using shadowcasting devices and glyph-lit constellations to unlock a second door.

4. Security Checkpoint Gamma (Guardian Hall)
(Designed by the Crimson Guard)
	• A kill corridor flanked by four armored statues, each animated with war-forged spirit cores.
	• Arcane cannons and dispel traps line the walls, calibrated to fire on unregistered magic.
	• A command crystal can temporarily deactivate defenses, but is located in a locked booth only accessible to a Guard commander.
	• The end of the hall has a pressure rune that must be stepped on with the precise rhythm of the Guard’s ceremonial march; failure triggers an explosive backlash.

5. Security Checkpoint Delta (Sigil’s Ward Hall)
(Designed by the Shaded Sigil)
	• A long hallway veiled in perpetual darkness—no light sources can penetrate except those attuned to Sigil glyphstones.
	• Mind-warping illusions and anti-teleport fields fill the space.
	• A floating, whispering archive—known as the Oracle Sigil—asks each entrant a question. If the answer is false, or if hesitation is detected, it locks the mind in a looping memory prison until an external override is performed.
	• A mirror of truth at the end reflects the soul; those with violent or traitorous intentions toward Rena cannot pass.

6. Final Chamber – The Core Vault
	• A circular chamber constructed of interlocking vault segments, like the petals of a stone flower.
	• The floor is made of velrathi glasssteel, smooth and semi-reflective, enchanted to detect lies or illusions.
	• The center holds:
		○ The Grand Ledger – a record of debts, state contracts, and magical favors owed or enforced by Rena.
		○ The Artifact Cellar – magically suspended objects, including imperial relics, cursed items, and magical documents too dangerous for public knowledge.
		○ Coin Vaults – with enchanted containers that weigh and magically brand every coin that leaves (to prevent laundering or tampering).
		○ The Three Seals – crystal shards, each belonging to one of the ruling factions, used to activate or override the entire system in emergencies.

Additional Defenses (Active & Passive)
	• Failsafe Sigil Lockdown: If all three Seals are removed or damaged, the entire vault collapses inward into a stasis loop, freezing all matter and time within for 100 years.
	• Silent Alarm System: Sends telepathic alerts to designated faction leaders and security mages; was not triggered during the heist.
	• Spectral Arbiters: Bound imperial spirits tasked with judgment—normally dormant but can be awakened by violating ancient oaths within the chamber.
	• Illusory Duplicates: Some corridors and doors are decoys meant to delay or trap infiltrators in endless loops.

name: The Corrupted Protectors
description: While investigating the vault, you came across some guards that are not normal
notes: While in the main chambers, guards will appear after some time
